deferred_follow_up: Verifier-owned parent presence and delegated budget admission have real mutation evidence, but universal delegated-authority validation remains DEFERRED-FOLLOW-UP. The conformance test rejects an unknown parent and accepts a registered parent while committing the child share. It does not recursively resolve complete parent lineage from an authoritative store, coordinate sibling budgets across kernel processes, or prove that every hosted, native, and trust-control entry point uses the strongest chain-binding verifier. Follow-up work must add authoritative recursive lineage resolution, distributed budget-state qualification, revocation-aware ancestry tests, and entry-point coverage.
note: Real partial mutation evidence. A positive control registers the parent with sufficient headroom, requires successful verification, and asserts that the child share is committed. Additional arms reject untrusted issuers, signed-body tampering, and expiry. A targeted cargo-mutants run replaced chio_kernel_core::capability_verify::admit_delegated_budget with Ok(()); the unknown-parent assertion caught the bypass. PARTIAL: recursive authoritative lineage, cross-process budget coordination, revocation-aware ancestry, and universal entry-point enforcement remain deferred.
